questions.question: What is the topic of the essay in the unit?

options.A: whether we should buy locally or buy from anywhere in the world

questions.correct_answer_text: whether we should buy locally or buy from anywhere in the world

steps: The essay asks whether we should buy local produce or buy from abroad.

questions.explanation: It weighs the two sides of the argument.

questions.question: Why is 'buying local' a good title for the essay?

options.A: it summarises the topic in just two words

questions.correct_answer_text: it summarises the topic in just two words

steps: 'Buying local' instantly tells the reader what the essay is about.
solution.summary: A good title is short and clear.

questions.explanation: It shows the subject immediately.

questions.question: Why should the opening paragraph do more than repeat the title?

options.A: it should also grab the reader's attention

questions.correct_answer_text: it should also grab the reader's attention

steps: A good opening catches the reader's attention and introduces the debate.

questions.explanation: Then introduce the issue being argued.

questions.question: In the opening paragraph, what example is used?

options.A: packaged food, books and cheap clothes

questions.correct_answer_text: packaged food, books and cheap clothes

steps: Packaged food, books and cheap clothes are given as examples.

questions.explanation: These are things we can buy from anywhere.

questions.question: What surprise does the opening paragraph mention?

options.A: a label showing that a product was made in another country
options.B: a price that is too cheap

questions.correct_answer_text: a label showing that a product was made in another country

steps: It is surprising when a label reveals a product was made far away.
solution.summary: A label shows a foreign origin.

questions.explanation: This surprises some buyers.

questions.question: What is a 'shop around'?

options.A: compare prices in different shops before buying

questions.correct_answer_text: compare prices in different shops before buying

steps: 'Shop around' means to compare prices before deciding.

questions.explanation: You shop around to find the best deal.

questions.question: What is 'to stock up'?

options.A: buy large quantities for the future

questions.correct_answer_text: buy large quantities for the future

steps: 'Stock up' means to buy a lot of something to keep for later.

questions.explanation: We stock up on essentials.

questions.question: What is 'to run errands'?

options.A: make short journeys to do jobs like buying things

questions.correct_answer_text: make short journeys to do jobs like buying things

steps: 'Run errands' means make short trips to do small tasks.

questions.explanation: Like going to the shop or the bank.

questions.question: What is 'to go on a shopping spree'?

options.A: go shopping and spend a lot of money in a short time

questions.correct_answer_text: go shopping and spend a lot of money in a short time

steps: A shopping spree means buying lots of things at once.

questions.explanation: It is an exciting but expensive activity.

questions.question: What does 'mooch around' mean?

options.A: wander slowly around the shops with no clear purpose

questions.correct_answer_text: wander slowly around the shops with no clear purpose

steps: 'Mooch around' means wander without a fixed aim.

questions.explanation: People mooch around the shops on Saturdays.

questions.question: Which phrase means 'exactly what I need'?

steps: 'Just the ticket' means exactly what is wanted or needed.

questions.explanation: A shopping-related idiom.

questions.question: What does 'weigh up the pros and cons' mean?

steps: 'Weigh up the pros and cons' means think about the good and bad points.

questions.explanation: This is the core of a for-and-against essay.

questions.question: In a for-and-against essay, where do you usually state your own opinion?

options.C: at the start of every sentence
options.D: in the middle of a list

steps: The essay generally ends with the writer's own opinion.

questions.explanation: You reach your conclusion at the end.

questions.question: What tense do you normally use to give your opinion at the end?

steps: Use the present simple when giving your own opinion.

questions.explanation: 'I think that...', 'In my opinion...'

questions.question: Why do you NOT use the past tense to give your final opinion?

options.A: opinions are about the present, not the past

questions.correct_answer_text: opinions are about the present, not the past

steps: A final opinion states what you think now, so the present simple fits.

questions.explanation: Present simple matches this.

questions.question: Which words help you paraphrase in an essay?

options.A: nearly the same as, identical, a different way to say

questions.correct_answer_text: nearly the same as, identical, a different way to say

steps: Paraphrasing words include 'nearly the same as' and 'a different way to say'.

questions.explanation: They help you avoid repeating words.

questions.question: Why is paraphrasing useful in an essay?

options.A: it lets you show the same idea in a different way

questions.correct_answer_text: it lets you show the same idea in a different way

steps: Paraphrasing expresses the same idea without repeating it.

questions.explanation: It keeps the essay natural.

questions.question: Which of these is a way to introduce a contrast?

steps: 'On the other hand' introduces the opposite side of an argument.

questions.explanation: Use it in a for-and-against essay.

questions.question: Which expression introduces a conclusion?

steps: 'Taking everything into account' signals the final opinion.

questions.explanation: Other options include 'on balance'.

questions.question: What does 'in my view' do in a final paragraph?

steps: 'In my view' clearly marks a personal opinion.

questions.explanation: Similar: 'I believe that', 'as I see it'.

questions.question: Which word means 'finally' or 'in conclusion'?

steps: 'Eventually' can mean finally, in the end.

questions.explanation: It signals the final paragraph.

questions.question: Which phrase means 'considering everything'?

steps: 'On balance' means when all things are considered.

questions.explanation: Used before giving a final opinion.

questions.question: Complete the essay opener: 'The internet means that we can now buy things ______ all over the world.'

steps: '...buy things from all over the world.'

questions.explanation: We buy things from places.

questions.question: Which argument FOR buying locally is given in the essay?

options.A: it protects jobs in your local community

questions.correct_answer_text: it protects jobs in your local community

steps: Buying local keeps money in the local community and protects jobs.

questions.explanation: Supporting local businesses helps your area.

questions.question: Which argument AGAINST buying locally is given in the essay?

options.A: local goods can be more expensive and limited in choice

questions.correct_answer_text: local goods can be more expensive and limited in choice

steps: Local products may cost more and the choice may be smaller.

questions.explanation: Foreign goods are often cheaper.

questions.question: What does 'exclusive' mean in 'exclusive goods'?

steps: 'Exclusive' means special, limited to certain places or people.

questions.explanation: An exclusive product is not mass-produced.

questions.question: What does 'high-end' mean?

steps: 'High-end' describes luxury, quality goods.

questions.explanation: High-end products cost more.

questions.question: What does 'globally' mean in the essay?

steps: 'Globally' means across the whole world.

questions.explanation: Goods can now be sold globally.

questions.question: What does 'imported' mean?

options.A: brought into a country from another

questions.correct_answer_text: brought into a country from another

steps: 'Imported' goods come from another country.

questions.explanation: Opposite: exported or local.

questions.question: Which word means 'exported'?

steps: 'Exported' means sold or sent to other countries.

questions.explanation: The opposite of imported.

questions.question: What is the basic structure of a for-and-against essay?

options.A: introduction, arguments for, arguments against, conclusion

questions.correct_answer_text: introduction, arguments for, arguments against, conclusion

steps: It has an opening, the two sides, and a final opinion.

questions.explanation: Each point is in its own paragraph.

questions.question: Why should each paragraph contain only ONE main idea?

options.A: it makes the argument clear to the reader
options.D: it is a rule of spelling

questions.correct_answer_text: it makes the argument clear to the reader

steps: One idea per paragraph keeps the essay clear and logical.

questions.explanation: Readers can follow the argument easily.

questions.question: Which linking word best adds another argument FOR?

steps: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point.

questions.explanation: Use 'however' to contrast.

questions.question: Which linking word best introduces an AGAINST point?

steps: 'However' introduces a point that contrasts with the last one.

questions.explanation: It signals the opposing view.

questions.question: Complete: 'The writer of a for-and-against essay should be ________ in the main paragraphs.'

steps: In the body you present both sides fairly; emotion comes in the conclusion.

questions.explanation: Only the final opinion is personal.

questions.question: What does 'cutting-edge' mean in 'cutting-edge technology'?

steps: 'Cutting-edge' means the newest and most advanced.

questions.explanation: Another phrase: state-of-the-art.

questions.question: Which phrase means 'the most fashionable'?

steps: 'Up to the minute' means the very latest.

questions.explanation: Used about fashion and news.

questions.question: What is the final paragraph mainly for?

steps: The last paragraph gives your personal conclusion.

questions.explanation: It balances everything together.

questions.question: In the model essay, what is the writer's final opinion?

options.A: it is best to strike a balance between local and imported goods

questions.correct_answer_text: it is best to strike a balance between local and imported goods

steps: The writer concludes we should strike a balance between the two.

questions.explanation: Buy local when possible, but accept imports too.

questions.question: Which word best completes: 'Buying local is good for the ________ economy.'

steps: 'The local economy' is the standard collocation.

questions.explanation: Buying local helps it grow.
